input_oneliner: 71F POD2 knee arthroplasty, Foley in, T 38.6 overnight, mild cough, no complaints otherwise

reference_targets_freetext.item: Respiratory rate; focal crackles, egophony, dullness, and bronchial breath sounds on lung auscultation
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Abnormal vital signs plus asymmetric lung findings are the best bedside predictors of pneumonia; normal vitals and exam lower probability

reference_targets_freetext.item: Inspect surgical wound for erythema, warmth, drainage, dehiscence, and tenderness beyond the incision
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Surgical site infection is common by day 2-5 and is entirely a bedside diagnosis

reference_targets_freetext.item: Costovertebral angle (CVA) tenderness and suprapubic tenderness; inspect the catheter site; ask about flank pain or rigors
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Catheter-associated UTI needs symptoms beyond bacteriuria; flank tenderness or rigors raise pyelonephritis

reference_targets_freetext.item: Calf circumference asymmetry >3 cm, calf tenderness, unilateral swelling
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Post-operative immobility makes DVT a real cause of low-grade fever

reference_targets_freetext.item: Ask: sputum, pleuritic chest pain, chills, new medications, transfusion, and incentive spirometry use
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Directs the differential and identifies drug fever or atelectasis as alternative explanations

should_not_recommend: Empiric broad-spectrum antibiotics before source exam
Attributing the fever to atelectasis without a source examination

perturbation_pair.expected_change: Intra-abdominal abscess or anastomotic leak enters the top differential; abdominal exam for distension, peritoneal signs, and wound inspection become must-have; lung exam stays but drops to should-still-include; ask about flatus, bowel function, and drain output rises.
